questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of open/closed principles, plugin registries, and runtime configurability for cross-cutting concerns like logging.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy pattern
- Registry / plugin architecture
- Thread-safety and dynamic configuration
- Separation of concerns in logging

## Code Example
```javascript
interface LogEvent { level: string; message: string; ts: number; }
interface LogFormatter { format(event: LogEvent): string; }
class JSONFormatter implements LogFormatter { format(e: LogEvent) { return JSON.stringify(e); } }
class KVFormatter implements LogFormatter { format(e: LogEvent) { return `ts=${e.ts} level=${e.level} msg='${e.message}'`; } }
class Registry<T> { private map = new Map<string, T>(); register(name: string, v: T){ this.map.set(name, v); } get(name: string): T | undefined { return this.map.get(name); } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle thread-safety in a multi-threaded environment?
- How to test registering and switching formatters in isolation?

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a runtime-extensible policy system with hot-reload and safe concurrent access in a high-throughput gateway. It probes how policies are composed per-route, how to avoid downtime during updates, and how to version or rollback policies.

Key Concepts

- Strategy/Policy pattern
- Registry and dynamic module loading
- Atomic swaps and concurrency control
- Per-route pipelines and cache invalidation

Code Example

```javascript
// Implementation sketch
export interface Policy {
  apply(req, ctx, next: () => Promise<void>): Promise<void>
}
export class PolicyRegistry {
  get(name: string): () => Policy
}
```

Follow-up Questions

- How would you test hot-reload safety and latency?
- How would you version policies and roll back on failure?

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests ability to design a runtime-extensible backend with a clean interface, minimal FAB (feature-flag) API, and safe runtime swapping.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy pattern for pluggable backends
- Registry for runtime extension
- Atomic swap and cache coherence trade-offs

```javascript
// Interfaces and usage sketch
interface IFlagBackend { getFlag(name:string, context?:any): boolean; }
class FlagCore { constructor(private backend:IFlagBackend){ } isEnabled(name:string, ctx?:any){ return this.backend.getFlag(name, ctx); } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test swapping backends without downtime?
- How would you implement per-tenant flags and cache invalidation?
